text.tspan: Even though Paraceratherium lacks a horn like it’s
relatively smaller horned cousins, we still know it’s
a member of the rhinoceros family. Look at those
teeth, the molars of the upper jaw have these pi
shaped grooves while the lower on
grooves. Paleontologists use this trait to tell if an
ancient animal is closely related to rhinos instead of
In fact the branch of the family tree Paraceratherium
belongs to is entirely hornless and
more like horses than any rhino. To m
stranger, they behaved like giraffes browsing at the
tops of trees where no other animal could reach.
